drills.name: Four-Station Skill Rotation
drills.desc: Divide the ice into four quadrants with one skill at each station. Groups of 3–5 players rotate every 4–5 minutes on the whistle. Demonstrate each station once, keep instructions short, and keep every player moving.
drills.pts:
Station 1: glide, stop and get up (balance and stopping)
Station 2: slalom through cones (edges, knee bend)
Station 3: carry the puck around cones to the end
Station 4: partner pass, then shoot on the small net
Rotate clockwise on the whistle; keep lines short

drills.name: Puck Pickup Relay
drills.equip: Pucks (20+), two small nets or cones
drills.desc: Scatter pucks around the center circle. Two teams line up at the end boards. On the whistle the first player on each team skates to the circle, picks up one puck with the stick, carries it back and shoots it into the team net, then tags the next player. The first team to collect all of its pucks wins.
drills.pts:
Head up while carrying the puck
One puck at a time; no pushing
Younger players can carry the puck by hand first, then with the stick
Add a cone to skate around for more challenge

drills.name: Follow the Leader Snake
drills.desc: The coach (or a confident skater) leads the group through a winding path while the players follow in a single line, copying the leader: marching, gliding, squatting low, one-foot glides, stops and starts. Swap leaders often so everyone gets a turn.
drills.pts:
Keep the head up and the stick on the ice
Mix speeds: slow, fast, freeze
The leader changes the skating style every few seconds
Everyone gets a turn at leading

drills.name: Face-Off Circle Tag
drills.desc: Players skate freely inside the two end-zone face-off circles. One or two taggers (wearing pinnies) try to tag the others with a hand tag. Tagged players do a quick tuck or sit and wait to be freed by a teammate, or become taggers. Add a puck for each player to build puck control.
drills.pts:
Eyes up and aware of space
Use edges to change direction
Add a puck to turn it into a puck-control game

drills.name: Shoot at the Targets
drills.equip: Pucks, 3-4 small nets or cone targets
drills.desc: 3-4 lines of players each shoot at a small net from about 20 feet. After a shot the player collects a puck from the pile and goes to the back of the next line. Move the shooting line back or add a target to aim at as shooting improves.
drills.pts:
Eyes on the target, not the puck
Weight moves from the back foot to the front foot
Follow through toward the target
Pick up a puck and move quickly: lots of shots

drills.name: Puck Control Maze
drills.desc: Scatter cones across the zone to make a maze. Each player carries a puck through the maze, changing direction around cones and keeping the head up. Add a second puck, a time challenge, or a final shot on net.
drills.pts:
Soft hands: cushion the puck with both hands on the stick
Head up: look past the puck
Small touches keep the puck close
Change speeds and direction

drills.name: Cross-Ice 3-on-3
drills.desc: Set two small nets on the side boards of a half-ice area and play 3-on-3 across the ice with no goalies. The coach feeds a new puck when the puck leaves the area or after a goal. Use short shifts (60–90 seconds) and run a second group in the other half of the rink.
drills.pts:
More pucks, more shots, more touches
Change on the whistle after about a minute
Always give the puck carrier a passing option
No set positions: players read the play

drills.name: Cone Weave & Shoot
drills.desc: Players start at the blue line with a puck, weave through three cones, and finish with a shot on net. The next player goes when the one ahead reaches the second cone. Add a coach or goalie as a screen to make the shot more game-like.
drills.pts:
Puck out front, head up between cones
Bend the knees and use inside edges on the turns
Accelerate out of the last cone and shoot in stride
Alternate lines so players shoot from both sides

drills.name: Sharks & Minnows
drills.desc: Minnows line up on one side with a puck each (no pucks for younger groups). Two sharks wait in the middle. On the whistle the minnows try to skate to the far side without losing their puck to a shark. Minnows who are tagged or lose the puck become sharks for the next round. Tip: use the library orientation controls to run it across the ice, parallel to the blue lines.
drills.pts:
Protect the puck with the body and stick
Look up to find open ice
Change directions with crossovers and quick turns
Last minnow standing wins

drills.name: Partner Passing on the Move
drills.desc: In pairs, players skate side by side down the ice passing the puck back and forth. Start with flat, soft passes at slow speed, then add speed. Progress to backhand passes, receiving on the move, and finish with a shot on net.
drills.pts:
Passer: look at the target and follow through
Receiver: show a stick target and cushion the puck
Keep about 15–20 feet between partners
Finish with a shot on net

drills.name: Half-Ice 3-on-3 Game
drills.desc: Play 3-on-3 on a half-ice area with a net (and goalie if available) at each end. Use short shifts (45–60 seconds) and have the coach restart play with a new puck. Emphasize support, give-and-go passes and quick shots.
drills.pts:
The puck carrier always has a teammate in support
Reward quick shots and rebounds
Change on the whistle after about a minute
Keep spacing: avoid three players in the same spot

drills.name: Give-and-Go to the Net
drills.desc: Two lines start near the blue line. Player 1 passes to Player 2, then skates to open ice; Player 2 returns the pass in stride and Player 1 shoots. Alternate sides and swap roles every few reps.
drills.pts:
Pass, then move to open ice immediately
Receive with soft hands and the blade open
Time the return pass to arrive in stride
Shoot while the goalie is still moving

drills.name: 2-on-1 Rush
drills.equip: Pucks, one net, goalie if available
drills.desc: Two forwards start at center ice and attack one defender who starts at the far blue line. The forwards attack with speed, keep the passing option open and decide to shoot or pass. Rotate so everyone plays forward and defense.
drills.pts:
Attackers: stay wide, keep the passing lane open
Defender: stay between the attackers, take away the pass
The shooter looks for rebounds
The second attacker drives the net

drills.name: Edge Work Circles
drills.desc: Players skate around the end-zone face-off circles: forward crossovers around one circle, backward crossovers around the other, switching direction at the whistle. Add pucks, tight turns and quick transitions for older groups.
drills.pts:
Deep knee bend, inside edge push
Eyes up, not at the feet
Stay on the circle line
Accelerate out of every turn

drills.name: Four-Corner Passing
drills.desc: Four lines form a square. The first player in each line passes to the next corner, then follows the pass and goes to the back of that line. Progress from one puck to two pucks, then add a shot at the end.
drills.pts:
Pass to the stick, not to the feet
Receive with the blade angled and the head up
Follow your pass
Call for the puck so partners know where you are

drills.name: Two-Line Shooting
drills.equip: Pucks, one net, goalie if available
drills.desc: Two lines start at the face-off dots, one on each side. The first player on the left skates the wing while the first player on the right passes; the shooter receives in stride and shoots. Switch lines every few reps.
drills.pts:
Pass firm and flat, to the stick side
Shooter: receive in stride and shoot through the net
Go to the net for rebounds
Switch sides so everyone shoots from both wings

drills.name: Triangle Passing
drills.desc: Three lines form a triangle. Each player passes to the next corner and follows the pass to the end of that line. Add a one-touch pass, a backhand pass, then a second puck going the opposite way.
drills.pts:
Pass and move: follow the pass
Receive with a stick target out front
Keep the puck on the ice with soft hands
Add speed once the passes are crisp

drills.name: 4-on-4 Net-Front Game
drills.desc: Four-on-four on half ice with goalies. A goal only counts if a player is at the net front or the shot is a rebound. Short shifts (60 seconds) keep the pace high. Focus on driving the net, screens and second efforts.
drills.pts:
Drive wide and attack the net
One player always at the net front
Win loose pucks with quick stick lifts
Communicate: call for the puck and name the pressure

drills.name: Defense-to-Defense Breakout
drills.desc: The coach dumps a puck into the corner. D1 retrieves and passes to D2 or up the boards to the winger; the center swings low to support. Start with no pressure, then add a passive forechecker, then a live one.
drills.pts:
Scan before the puck arrives
Pass to the tape: firm, flat passes
Wingers present stick targets on the boards
Center supports low and reads the pressure

drills.name: 3-on-2 Continuous Rush
drills.desc: Three forwards attack two defenders. After the shot the two defenders become attackers with a third player joining from the neutral zone as the next group goes the other way.
drills.pts:
Forwards: width and depth, shoot with a purpose
Defense: stay in front, gap up and talk
The late player trails to create the third option
Quick transition when the puck changes hands

drills.name: 1-on-1 Angling & Gap Control
drills.desc: A forward carries the puck through the neutral zone against a defender. The defender controls the gap, angles the attacker toward the boards and closes with the stick and body. Switch roles every rep.
drills.pts:
Defender: keep the gap, eyes on the chest
Angle the attacker to the boards
Close the gap on the last two strides
Attacker: protect the puck and read the gap

drills.name: 2-on-2 Corner Battle
drills.desc: Two players from each team battle for a puck in the corner. Whoever wins possession attacks the net with support from the other player. Use pads to keep the area tight and switch pairs every 40 seconds.
drills.pts:
Body position first: gain inside position
Stick on puck, strong on skates
Quick support to the puck winner
Compete for 40 seconds, then rotate

drills.name: Neutral-Zone Regroup
drills.desc: The defense retrieves a puck, passes back to the partner, and the team regroups through the neutral zone with speed before attacking. Emphasize support, spacing and attacking with speed through the middle.
drills.pts:
Defensemen pivot and use the net as a regroup point
Forwards swing wide and come back with speed
Pass early to a moving target
Enter the zone with possession

drills.name: Shooting Circuit – Three Stations
drills.desc: Three shooting stations around the zone: a slot shot off a pass, a quick release from the wing, and a rebound/tip at the net front. Groups rotate after each rep and after a set time.
drills.pts:
Shoot with a purpose: pick a corner
Quick release: pull the puck and fire in stride
Get to the net front for rebounds
Rotate stations every 3 minutes

drills.name: Breakout: Strong-Side Overload
drills.desc: The strong-side winger, center and defense form an overload to get the puck out of the zone under pressure. Add a live forechecker and then a second forechecker once the pattern is clean.
drills.pts:
Quick support within 15 feet of the puck
Use the boards and quick give-and-go passes
Weak-side forward stays high as an outlet
Support and communicate

drills.name: 2-1-2 Forecheck
drills.desc: F1 pressures the puck carrier, F2 supports and takes away the pass, F3 reads and covers the slot, defense hold the blue line. Walk through the structure, then go live with a forechecking group against a breakout group.
drills.pts:
F1: angle the carrier to the boards
F2: close the nearest outlet
F3: read and take the middle
Defense: step up when possession changes

drills.name: Three-Man Weave
drills.desc: Three forwards skate down the ice passing the puck and following their pass behind the next player in a weaving pattern, finishing with a shot. Add a defender or quick shot at the end to make it game-like.
drills.pts:
Follow your pass: pass and go behind the receiver
Keep spacing about 15 feet
Receive with soft hands and the blade open
Finish with a shot on net

drills.name: Power Play 1-3-1 Setup
drills.desc: Walk through the 1-3-1 structure against four penalty killers: one at the top, three across the middle, one low. Move the puck quickly, look for seams, and work the shot-and-screen play.
drills.pts:
Quick puck movement forces the PK out of position
Shooters pick a spot; net-front screens the goalie
Low player stays mobile behind the net
Rotate positions every few reps

drills.name: Slot One-Timers
drills.desc: A passer on the half wall feeds a shooter at the top of the slot for a one-timer. Shooters then rotate to the passing line and passers rotate to the shooting line. Add a screen or a second shooter for a rebound.
drills.pts:
Shooter: stick on the ice, show a target, shoot through the puck
Passer: firm pass on the stick side
Get to the net for the rebound
Rotate every few reps

drills.name: Defensive Zone Coverage – Box + 1
drills.desc: Four defenders form a box around the slot with one high player against five attackers who move the puck around the perimeter. Practice sliding to pressure the puck, sticks in lanes and clearing rebounds.
drills.pts:
Sticks in lanes and eyes on the puck and the man
Pressure the shooter and block lanes
Communicate switches and screens
Clear the puck quickly when you win it

drills.name: 4-on-4 Transition Game
drills.desc: Four-on-four on half ice with a quick transition rule: once a team gains possession they must make one pass before they can shoot. Short, intense shifts of 45–60 seconds.
drills.pts:
Quick, accurate first pass after the turnover
Support the puck carrier with speed
Defenders talk early to pick up loose forwards
Finish with a shot on net

drills.name: Net-Front & Tip Circuit
drills.desc: A point shot with a screen and a tip. The defender shoots through traffic, the forward screens the goalie, and a second forward looks to tip or rebound.
drills.pts:
Shoot low and on net
Screener: stick on the ice, eyes on the puck
Tipper: stay on the stick side of the shooter
Go for second chances

drills.name: Penalty Kill – Diamond
drills.desc: Four penalty killers in a diamond rotate with the puck while the power play moves it around the perimeter. Work on sticks in lanes, pressure at the right times and clearing the puck.
drills.pts:
Stay compact, sticks in lanes
Pressure when the puck is received
Clear the puck quickly and cleanly
Communicate on every switch

drills.name: Offensive Zone Cycle
drills.desc: Three forwards and a defender cycle the puck in the corner. Pass low to high, rotate through the high slot, and finish with a point shot or net-front tip.
drills.pts:
Protect the puck with the body
Cycle low to high and drive the net
Support the puck carrier within 10 feet
Finish with a shot and second effort

drills.name: Timing Rush: Wide Drive
drills.desc: The defense breaks out with a pass to the winger; the near winger drives wide, the center fills the middle lane and the late forward trails. Attack with speed and shoot with purpose.
drills.pts:
Wide drive forces the defense to back up
Center takes the middle lane with speed
Trailer arrives late for the second option
Execute with tempo

drills.name: Offensive Zone Faceoff Plays
drills.desc: Practice faceoff plays in the offensive zone: win the draw back to the defense for a shot with a screen, or win it to the winger for a quick shot. Rotate through the formations.
drills.pts:
Center: win the draw back to the defense
Defense: read the draw and step into the shot
Winger: screen or tip near the net
Rotate players every 3 reps

drills.name: 1-2-2 Forecheck
drills.desc: F1 pressures and angles the puck carrier, the two wingers form a wall to take away the outlets, and the defense hold the blue line. Walk through the structure, then go live.
drills.pts:
F1: angle and take away the middle
Wingers: pinch and close the boards
Defense: gap up on the blue line
Switch positions each rep

drills.name: Continuous 3-on-3 Compete
drills.desc: Continuous three-on-three on half ice with goalies. Winners stay on; losers do a quick conditioning skate. Keep shifts short and emphasize compete level.
drills.pts:
Win battles and take away time and space
Quick transitions on loose pucks
Support the puck carrier
Short, intense shifts

drills.name: Border Tag
drills.equip: A row of 1×10 ft pads (or sticks and cones) for the divider, pinnies for chasers
drills.desc: Lay a row of pads across the middle of the zone as a divider. Players pair up with one on each side: the chaser tries to tag the runner by reaching across the divider, and the runner keeps moving to stay out of reach. Swap roles on the whistle and run several pairs along the divider at once.
drills.pts:
Stop, start and change direction with sharp edges
Head up: watch the runner’s hips, not the stick
Fake one way, then go the other
Swap chaser and runner often so everyone gets reps

drills.name: Puck Knockout
drills.equip: One puck per player, cones to mark the zone, pinnies for knockers, a tire
drills.desc: Mark a zone with cones. Everyone inside has a puck except one or two knockers, who try to knock pucks out of the zone. A player whose puck is knocked out collects it, circles the tire outside and jumps straight back in, so nobody sits out.
drills.pts:
Head up: see who is coming before they arrive
Shield the puck with your body and stick
Keep moving: no standing still
Knockers: poke from the side and stay on your feet

inspired.text: ADM Kids: “Three Games for Optimal Development at 8U”

objects.text: Knocked out? Circle the tire and jump back in

drills.name: Tire Tug of War
drills.equip: A tire (or cone cluster or large ball), 20 or more pucks
drills.desc: Two teams each stay along one long side of the zone with a tire in the middle. On “go”, each team shoots pucks at the tire to push it toward the other team’s side. A team scores when the tire crosses the opposite line. Players stay on their own side, collecting pucks and shooting as fast as they can.
drills.pts:
Aim at the tire, not at the other team
Pick up another puck and shoot again quickly
Use forehand and backhand shots
Reset the tire to the middle after each point

inspired.text: ADM Kids: “Three Games for Optimal Development at 8U”

drills.name: Six-Pack 2v2
drills.equip: Six tires (goals), pucks or a ball, pinnies
drills.desc: Split the ice into six zones with a tire as the goal in each. Play 2v2 in every zone in 30–40 second shifts, then rotate partners. A team scores by hitting the tire with the puck. Younger players can use a ball or ring instead of a puck.
drills.pts:
Short shifts: change on the whistle
Always have a teammate close to help
Shoot at the tire from anywhere
Rotate partners so everyone plays with everyone

inspired.text: Hockey Alberta: Learn to Play Skill Development Guidebook

drills.name: Shrinking Pond
drills.equip: One puck per player, extra pucks for the coach, cones for the pond
drills.desc: Everyone skates with a puck inside a small pond marked with cones. Every 20–30 seconds the coach takes a few pucks away, so some players have to steal a puck to get back in the game. Keep the pond small, praise heads-up skating, and finish with a quick free-puck celebration.
drills.pts:
Protect the puck with your body and stick
Head up: find open ice
No puck? Pressure someone, then steal
Everyone keeps moving

inspired.text: How To Hockey: “OMHA Novice / Squirt Hockey Drills”

drills.name: Tire Turn Bulldog
drills.equip: Two tires, a puck for each runner (optional), pinnies for the bulldogs
drills.desc: Runners line up along one side boards, each with a puck; one or two bulldogs wait in the middle. Before crossing, each runner must circle a tire with a tight control turn, then escape across the ice without losing the puck. Runners who are caught join the bulldogs for the next round.
drills.pts:
Low and tight on the turn: push with the inside edge
Look for gaps: head up
Keep the puck on the boards side, away from the bulldog
Bulldogs: angle the runner, do not just chase

inspired.text: Ice Hockey Systems: “U10 - 3 Station Practice Plan #3”

drills.name: Gate Rush
drills.equip: Twelve cones for six gates, one puck, pinnies
drills.desc: Set six gates (two cones about 6 feet apart) around the zone. Play 3v3 or 4v4: a team scores by passing the puck through any gate to a teammate on the other side. The same gate cannot be used twice in a row, which keeps both teams hunting for open space.
drills.pts:
Move to open space after you pass
Call for the puck with your voice and your stick
Defenders: close the lanes instead of chasing
Keep your head up to scan the gates

objects.text: Score by passing through a gate

drills.name: Net-Front Battle
drills.equip: Pucks, a net, a feeder (coach or player)
drills.desc: One attacker and one defender battle in front of the net. The feeder at the point shoots or passes pucks toward the net; the attacker screens, tips and pounds rebounds while the defender clears the attacker’s stick and then the loose puck. Score a point for a goal or a clean clear, and rotate every 30 seconds.
drills.pts:
Attacker: stick on the ice, eyes on the shot, look for the rebound
Defender: take away the attacker’s stick first, then the puck
Be strong on your skates, not just with your hands
Play to the whistle for second chances

drills.name: Hub Net 2v2
drills.equip: Two small or medium nets, pinnies, pucks
drills.desc: Put two nets back to back in the middle of a small marked area. Two teams of two can score on either net, so play flows around the nets and every player has to read where the pressure is. Use 45-second shifts and a new puck after every goal to keep the pace high.
drills.pts:
Look for the back-door play
Protect the puck on your body side
Talk: who has the puck, who is open
Defend by taking away the closest passing lane

inspired.text: USA Hockey: small-area games article (corner, net-front and net-middle battles)

drills.name: Two-Pond 3v3
drills.equip: Four small nets, pinnies, two pucks
drills.desc: Split the ice into two ponds with a small net at each end of each pond, and run two 3v3 games side by side. On the whistle the players swap with a waiting group at center ice, so everyone gets short, hard shifts.
drills.pts:
Short shifts: go hard, then swap on the whistle
Support the puck carrier
Shoot early and look for rebounds
Waiting group: be ready to jump on

drills.name: Gap Lanes 2v2
drills.equip: Three 1×10 ft pads (or cones) for the center barrier, pucks
drills.desc: A row of pads down the middle of the neutral zone blocks the middle lane. Two forwards attack two defenders through the lanes on either side. The defenders have to hold a good gap, angle the puck carriers toward the boards and shut the pass across the barrier. Switch roles after every rep.
drills.pts:
Defenders: keep your gap and watch the attacker’s chest
Pivot and close the outside lane together
Attackers: create width and make the quick pass around the barrier
Finish with a shot or a regroup

inspired.text: Ice Hockey Systems: “U12 - Defensive Skills & Pressuring the Puck”

drills.name: Wave 3v3
drills.equip: A net and goalie, pinnies for three groups, pucks
drills.desc: Three attackers play three defenders in the zone while the next attacking group waits at the blue line. When the whistle blows, or the defense wins the puck and clears it, the waiting group enters, the old attackers become the defenders, and the old defenders go to the back of the line. The defense has to gap up as each new wave arrives.
drills.pts:
Defense: gap up as the next wave enters
Attackers: use speed and support to get a shot quickly
Quick transition: when the puck changes hands, go
Communicate: call the group you are covering

objects.text: Next wave waits at the blue line

drills.name: 4-on-3 Quick Hits
drills.equip: A net and goalie, pinnies, pucks
drills.desc: Four attackers play three defenders in the zone in 45-second shifts. The attackers move the puck to the open player and get shots through traffic; the defenders block lanes and clear the puck. After each shift, rotate: attackers to defense, defenders out, a new four in.
drills.pts:
Attackers: quick puck movement to the open player
Shoot through traffic and go for rebounds
Defenders: sticks in lanes and take away the seam pass
Clear the puck and change on the whistle

drills.name: Getting Up and Basic Stance
drills.desc: Gather the players around the coach. Show the athletic stance: knees and ankles bent, back straight, head up, stick on the ice. Rock forward and back, lean side to side, and hop. Then practice lying down, rolling onto the stomach, getting to the knees and standing up into the stance.
drills.pts:
Knees and ankles bent, chest up, head up
Rock forward and back to find the balance point
Roll, knees, then stand
Coaches move through the group to fix stances

drills.name: T-Push Scoot
drills.desc: Players line up along a line or the boards with the back skate turned to form a "T" behind the front skate. They push down and out with the back skate, gliding on the front one and finishing the push with the toe. Skate the length of the zone one push at a time, then switch feet.
drills.pts:
Back skate makes a T behind the front skate
Push all the way until the leg is straight
Bring the pushing foot back under the body
Switch feet and repeat

drills.name: C-Cuts
drills.desc: Players line up along the boards. Gliding on one skate, they push a C-shaped cut across the ice with the other, then bring that foot back under the body. Do three or four on one foot, switch, then alternate feet.
drills.pts:
Glide on a bent knee
Push out in a C shape, then recover the foot to the middle
Alternate feet only after a full recovery
Keep the head up

drills.name: Simon Says on Skates
drills.desc: Players scatter with the coach in front. The coach calls skills such as balancing on one foot, jumping on one or two feet, touching knees or toes, or falling to the knees and getting back up. Players only do the move when the coach says "Simon says".
drills.pts:
Balance with a low, steady stance
Get up quickly after every fall to the knees
Make it silly and keep everyone moving
Coaches circulate and praise good balance

drills.name: Don’t Wake the Giant
drills.equip: A pile of pucks or balls, 1 coach
drills.desc: A coach is the giant guarding a treasure of pucks and keeps falling asleep. Players tiptoe and glide up, take a puck without waking the giant, and sneak back. When the giant wakes up, everyone skates away fast. Swap the giant often.
drills.pts:
Quiet, slow skating on the way in
Fast escape when the giant wakes
Take one puck at a time
Change giants so players get a turn

drills.name: Fetch
drills.equip: Tennis balls (one per player), no sticks
drills.desc: Players are dogs and play without sticks. The coach rolls out one tennis ball for every player. Dogs chase a ball, pick it up and bring it back to the coach, then bark. Some players may fetch several times and others once, and that is fine.
drills.pts:
No sticks, so hands are free to pick up the ball
Head up to find the next ball
Barking is encouraged
Roll balls in different directions

objects.text: Chase, pick up, bring it back

drills.name: Glides: Two Feet, One Foot
drills.desc: Players line up along the boards or a goal line, take a few strides and glide on two skates in the basic stance, then stand tall and return to the stance. Next they try one-foot glides, first leaning on the boards, then free, gliding as far as they can on each skate.
drills.pts:
Stay low in the stance while gliding
Try to glide farther each time
Lean on the boards to find one-foot balance first
Switch feet

objects.text: Stride, then glide as far as you can

drills.name: Edge Control Circle
drills.equip: Pucks laid in a quarter circle
drills.desc: Lay pucks in a path along a quarter of a face-off circle. Players take a few strides, then glide on the left skate on the inside edge, following the path around without putting the other skate down. Return on the outside edge, then repeat on the right skate.
drills.pts:
Lean into the circle and stay on one skate
Inside edge going out, outside edge coming back
Form a line on the far side
Repeat on the other foot

All skate the same direction

Push until the leg is fully extended
Recover the foot low to the ice

Stop at each puck before picking it up

Soft hands, puck stays close

Head up while the puck stays close

sheets.desc: Split the ice into six zones with a tire as the goal in each. Play 2v2 in every zone in 30–40 second shifts, then rotate partners. A team scores by hitting the tire with the puck. Younger players can use a ball or ring instead of a puck.
sheets.pts:
Short shifts: change on the whistle
Always have a teammate close to help
Shoot at the tire from anywhere
Rotate partners so everyone plays with everyone
sheets.equip: Six tires (goals), pucks or a ball, pinnies

sheets.title: Shrinking Pond
sheets.desc: Everyone skates with a puck inside a small pond marked with cones. Every 20–30 seconds the coach takes a few pucks away, so some players have to steal a puck to get back in the game. Keep the pond small, praise heads-up skating, and finish with a quick free-puck celebration.
sheets.pts:
Protect the puck with your body and stick
Head up: find open ice
No puck? Pressure someone, then steal
Everyone keeps moving
sheets.equip: One puck per player, extra pucks for the coach, cones for the pond

sheets.title: Face-Off Circle Tag
sheets.desc: Players skate freely inside the two end-zone face-off circles. One or two taggers (wearing pinnies) try to tag the others with a hand tag. Tagged players do a quick tuck or sit and wait to be freed by a teammate, or become taggers. Add a puck for each player to build puck control.
sheets.pts:
Eyes up and aware of space
Use edges to change direction
Add a puck to turn it into a puck-control game
sheets.equip: Pinnies for taggers (optional)

templates.name: 8U Station Practice
templates.goals: Build skating and puck skills in small groups, using stations and small-area games on a shared sheet of ice.
templates.blurb: A skating warm-up, four stations on one sheet with notes for each, then cross-ice games.

sheets.title: Warm-up: Sharks & Minnows
sheets.desc: Minnows line up on one side with a puck each (no pucks for younger groups). Two sharks wait in the middle. On the whistle the minnows try to skate to the far side without losing their puck to a shark. Minnows who are tagged or lose the puck become sharks for the next round. Tip: use the library orientation controls to run it across the ice, parallel to the blue lines.
sheets.pts:
Protect the puck with the body and stick
Look up to find open ice
Change directions with crossovers and quick turns
Last minnow standing wins
sheets.equip: Pinnies for sharks (pucks optional)

sheets.title: Four-station rotation
sheets.desc: Four stations on one sheet of ice. Split the players into four groups and rotate clockwise every six minutes on the whistle.
sheets.pts:
Rotate clockwise on the whistle
Keep the groups small so everyone is moving
Show the station before the whistle, then let them play
sheets.equip: 1) A row of 1×10 ft pads (or sticks and cones) for the divider, pinnies for chasers; 2) One puck per player, cones to mark the zone, pinnies for knockers, a tire; 3) A tire (or cone cluster or large ball), 20 or more pucks; 4) Pucks, three small nets or cone targets

areas.name: 1 Border Tag
areas.notes:
Border Tag – Lay a row of pads across the middle of the zone as a divider.
Stop, start and change direction with sharp edges
Head up: watch the runner’s hips, not the stick

areas.name: 2 Puck Knockout
areas.notes:
Puck Knockout – Mark a zone with cones.
Head up: see who is coming before they arrive
Shield the puck with your body and stick

areas.name: 3 Tire Tug of War
areas.notes:
Tire Tug of War – Two teams each stay along one long side of the zone with a tire in the middle.
Aim at the tire, not at the other team
Pick up another puck and shoot again quickly

areas.name: 4 Shoot at the Targets
areas.notes:
Shoot at the Targets – Three lines of players each shoot at a small net from about 20 feet.
Eyes on the target, not the puck
Weight moves from the back foot to the front foot

sheets.title: Cross-Ice 3-on-3
sheets.desc: Set two small nets on the side boards of a half-ice area and play 3-on-3 across the ice with no goalies. The coach feeds a new puck when the puck leaves the area or after a goal. Use short shifts (60–90 seconds) and run a second group in the other half of the rink.
sheets.pts:
More pucks, more shots, more touches
Change on the whistle after about a minute
Always give the puck carrier a passing option
No set positions: players read the play
sheets.equip: Two small nets, pinnies, pucks

sheets.title: Closing game: Two-Pond 3v3
sheets.desc: Split the ice into two ponds with a small net at each end of each pond, and run two 3v3 games side by side. On the whistle the players swap with a waiting group at center ice, so everyone gets short, hard shifts.
sheets.pts:
Short shifts: go hard, then swap on the whistle
Support the puck carrier
Shoot early and look for rebounds
Waiting group: be ready to jump on
sheets.equip: Four small nets, pinnies, two pucks

sheets.title: Gate Rush
sheets.desc: Set six gates (two cones about 6 feet apart) around the zone. Play 3v3 or 4v4: a team scores by passing the puck through any gate to a teammate on the other side. The same gate cannot be used twice in a row, which keeps both teams hunting for open space.
sheets.pts:
Move to open space after you pass
Call for the puck with your voice and your stick
Defenders: close the lanes instead of chasing
Keep your head up to scan the gates
sheets.equip: Twelve cones for six gates, one puck, pinnies

objects.text: Score by passing through a gate

sheets.title: Net-Front Battle
sheets.desc: One attacker and one defender battle in front of the net. The feeder at the point shoots or passes pucks toward the net; the attacker screens, tips and pounds rebounds while the defender clears the attacker’s stick and then the loose puck. Score a point for a goal or a clean clear, and rotate every 30 seconds.
sheets.pts:
Attacker: stick on the ice, eyes on the shot, look for the rebound
Defender: take away the attacker’s stick first, then the puck
Be strong on your skates, not just with your hands
Play to the whistle for second chances
sheets.equip: Pucks, a net, a feeder (coach or player)

sheets.title: Hub Net 2v2
sheets.desc: Put two nets back to back in the middle of a small marked area. Two teams of two can score on either net, so play flows around the nets and every player has to read where the pressure is. Use 45-second shifts and a new puck after every goal to keep the pace high.
sheets.pts:
Look for the back-door play
Protect the puck on your body side
Talk: who has the puck, who is open
Defend by taking away the closest passing lane
sheets.equip: Two small or medium nets, pinnies, pucks

sheets.title: 2-on-2 Corner Battle
sheets.desc: Two players from each team battle for a puck in the corner. Whoever wins possession attacks the net with support from the other player. Use pads to keep the area tight and switch pairs every 40 seconds.
sheets.pts:
Body position first: gain inside position
Stick on puck, strong on skates
Quick support to the puck winner
Compete for 40 seconds, then rotate
sheets.equip: Pucks, 1×10 ft pads (optional), net

templates.name: 12U Transition Day
templates.goals: Make quick decisions in transition: control the gap, support the puck and move it up ice.
templates.blurb: Edge work, then gap control, support and moving the puck up ice, finishing with a 4-on-4 game.

sheets.title: Edge Work Circles
sheets.desc: Players skate around the end-zone face-off circles: forward crossovers around one circle, backward crossovers around the other, switching direction at the whistle. Add pucks, tight turns and quick transitions for older groups.
sheets.pts:
Deep knee bend, inside edge push
Eyes up, not at the feet
Stay on the circle line
Accelerate out of every turn
sheets.equip: None

sheets.title: Gap Lanes 2v2
sheets.desc: A row of pads down the middle of the neutral zone blocks the middle lane. Two forwards attack two defenders through the lanes on either side. The defenders have to hold a good gap, angle the puck carriers toward the boards and shut the pass across the barrier. Switch roles after every rep.
sheets.pts:
Defenders: keep your gap and watch the attacker’s chest
Pivot and close the outside lane together
Attackers: create width and make the quick pass around the barrier
Finish with a shot or a regroup
sheets.equip: Three 1×10 ft pads (or cones) for the center barrier, pucks

sheets.title: Wave 3v3
sheets.desc: Three attackers play three defenders in the zone while the next attacking group waits at the blue line. When the whistle blows, or the defense wins the puck and clears it, the waiting group enters, the old attackers become the defenders, and the old defenders go to the back of the line. The defense has to gap up as each new wave arrives.
sheets.pts:
Defense: gap up as the next wave enters
Attackers: use speed and support to get a shot quickly
Quick transition: when the puck changes hands, go
Communicate: call the group you are covering
sheets.equip: A net and goalie, pinnies for three groups, pucks

objects.text: Next wave waits at the blue line

sheets.title: Neutral-Zone Regroup
sheets.desc: The defense retrieves a puck, passes back to the partner, and the team regroups through the neutral zone with speed before attacking. Emphasize support, spacing and attacking with speed through the middle.
sheets.pts:
Defensemen pivot and use the net as a regroup point
Forwards swing wide and come back with speed
Pass early to a moving target
Enter the zone with possession
sheets.equip: Pucks, cones

sheets.title: Closing game: 4-on-4
sheets.desc: Four-on-four on half ice with goalies. A goal only counts if a player is at the net front or the shot is a rebound. Short shifts (60 seconds) keep the pace high. Focus on driving the net, screens and second efforts.
sheets.pts:
Drive wide and attack the net
One player always at the net front
Win loose pucks with quick stick lifts
Communicate: call for the puck and name the pressure
sheets.equip: Two nets, pinnies, pucks
